chief_complaint: very dry eyes, dry mouth, and joint pain
hpi_details: 40F presents with a 1-year history of a persistent 'sand in my eyes' feeling and such severe dry mouth she cannot eat dry crackers without water. She also has generalized aching in her joints.
concerns: worried about dental cavities from dry mouth

core_concepts: Autoimmune destruction of exocrine glands (salivary, lacrimal) causing keratoconjunctivitis sicca and xerostomia.
diagnostic_clues: Dry mouth (needs water to swallow dry food)
common_misconceptions: Assuming dry eyes/mouth in an older patient is just age-related or medication-induced without checking serologies if it is severe.
dangerous_errors: Missing the increased risk for B-cell lymphoma (especially if patient presents with a new firm parotid mass).
management_principles: Confirm clinically and with appropriate objective testing/serology (including anti-Ro/SSA); provide preservative-free artificial tears, oral hydration and dental prevention. Secretagogues require clinician review for contraindications. Persistent or firm parotid enlargement, lymphadenopathy, fever, or weight loss warrants prompt evaluation for lymphoma.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Clinical Guidance

reference_soap.subjective: 40F with severe sicca symptoms (dry eyes, dry mouth) and arthralgias.
reference_soap.objective: Dry mucous membranes, absent salivary pooling. Bilateral parotid gland enlargement.
reference_soap.assessment: Suspected Sjogren's syndrome; bilateral parotid enlargement also requires assessment for alternative causes and lymphoma risk.
reference_soap.plan: Check anti-Ro/SSA, ANA and objective sicca testing as appropriate. Recommend preservative-free artificial tears, frequent hydration and dental referral. Promptly assess persistent/firm gland swelling, lymphadenopathy, fever, or weight loss.

learning_objectives: Identify the classic clinical features of Sjogren's Syndrome.

teaching.one_liner: A middle-aged female with profound dry eyes, dry mouth, and parotid enlargement.

must_ask.say: Do your eyes feel gritty, like there's sand in them?
Is your mouth so dry that you need water to swallow dry food like crackers?
How long have you had these dry eyes and dry mouth symptoms?
Have you noticed any swelling in front of your ears or under your jaw?
Have you had any joint aches along with the dryness?

history.answer: I have been dealing with severe dry eyes, a terribly dry mouth, and aching in my joints.
It started very slowly about a year ago, and it has gradually become worse over time.
My eyes constantly feel like I have sand or grit stuck in them, and they burn and get red easily.
My mouth is so completely dry that I cannot swallow dry crackers or bread without taking sips of water.
I have a dull, generalized ache across my hands, wrists, and knees that has been lingering for months.
The sides of my face right in front of and below my ears have felt puffy and slightly swollen for a few months.
Dry indoor air and working in front of a computer screen make my eyes burn worse. Drinking water helps for a second, but my mouth dries out immediately.
I do not have trouble swallowing liquids or soft food, only dry solid foods because there is no saliva to moisten them.
My skin feels drier than usual, and I have also had significant vaginal dryness.
No, my fingers do not turn white, blue, or numb when exposed to cold temperatures.
No, I have not had any butterfly rashes on my cheeks, unusual skin spots, or sensitivity to the sun.
No, I do not have any cough, wheezing, or shortness of breath.
No, I have not had any fevers, chills, or night sweats at all.
My weight has been completely steady, though I do feel more tired and drained than usual.
Other than the puffiness around my jaw, I have not noticed any hard lumps or swollen lymph nodes in my neck, armpits, or groin.
I have never had dry eyes or dry mouth like this before, and I haven't seen a doctor or had blood tests for it yet.
I carry a water bottle everywhere and tried regular over-the-counter lubricating eye drops, but they provide only momentary relief.
I do not take allergy medicines, cold syrups, sleeping aids, or antidepressants that could cause dryness.
It makes it hard to focus at work because my eyes burn while looking at the computer, and eating dry meals is very difficult.
I was wondering if I am just severely dehydrated or not drinking enough fluids throughout the day.
I am very worried that having such a dry mouth for so long will ruin my teeth and cause cavities.
I am hoping you can prescribe good eye drops and treatments to help restore moisture and ease the joint ache.
I have no chronic medical conditions, no high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid disease.
I have never had any operations and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications, regular over-the-counter pills, or vitamins.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked in my life.
I only have an occasional glass of wine once or twice a month with dinner.
I work as an office accountant and live with my husband and our ten-year-old daughter.
No one in my family has autoimmune conditions like lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, or Sjogren's, and no one has lymphoma.
My menstrual cycles are regular every 28 days, my last period started two weeks ago, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, comfortable, well-nourished woman appearing her stated age in no acute distress.
Mild bilateral conjunctival injection without discharge; sclerae are anicteric.
Bilateral conjunctival hyperemia with visibly diminished tear meniscus; pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light.
Dry, sticky oral mucous membranes with absent sublingual salivary pooling; tongue appears dry and slightly fissured without thrush or ulcers.
Soft, diffuse, non-tender bilateral parotid gland enlargement without discrete firm nodules; no cervical lymphadenopathy.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal vesicular breath sounds and no crackles or wheezes.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops appreciated.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended; no hepatosplenomegaly or palpable masses.
Mild diffuse tenderness across bilateral wrist, MCP, and PIP joints without visible swelling, warmth, erythema, or deformity.
Mildly dry skin overall without rashes, malar erythema, purpura, or photosensitivity lesions.
